item.title: Uniform Non-Deterministic Semantics for Ciuciura's $mbC^n$-Hierarchy
item.description: arXiv:2610.40797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a uniform non-deterministic semantics for the hierarchy of paraconsistent systems mbC^n introduced by Ciuciura. The proposed construction generalizes Omori's three-valued semantics for mbC^1 to all systems of the hierarchy. We prove soundness and completeness of the semantics with respect to the corresponding axiomatizations and show that the consequence relations of the systems mbC^n cannot be characterized by finite deterministic matrices.
item.dc:creator: Ela Drozdowska, Pawel Pawlowski

item.title: On Some Logics Intermediate Between S4.2 and S4.3 Defined by the Notion of Independence
item.description: arXiv:2610.40800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hamkins and Loewe described modal logic S4.2 through the notion of sets of independent buttons - statements that are possibly necessary - and switches - necessarily contingent statements. In this article we investigate logics intermediate between S4.2 and S4.3 that are defined through a different notion of independence. We provide an axiomatic description of such logics, state some basic facts and prove various completeness and decidability results.
item.dc:creator: Maciej A. Ha{\l}apacz (University of Wroc{\l}aw)

item.title: A Basic Modal Logic for the Abstract Treatment of Quantum Mixed States
item.description: arXiv:2610.40803v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum logic has developed in various directions since its inception. However, many existing logical approaches either focus only on pure states, or use Hilbert-space models in which the abstract relationship between pure states, mixed states, and probabilities is not made explicit. In this work, we introduce a model designed to handle quantum mixed states abstractly. Furthermore, we construct a proof system for the proposed logic and establish its completeness with respect to the intended semantics.
item.dc:creator: Tomoaki Kawano (Kanagawa University)

item.title: On the Reconstruction of Orthomodular Logic via Restricted Negation
item.description: arXiv:2610.40807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Orthomodular logic has long been studied as a fundamental logical framework within quantum logic. In addition to its lattice-theoretic foundations, various formulations have been proposed that incorporate specialized implication connectives and more complex logical connectives. In this study, we reconstruct orthomodular logic by introducing a connective referred to as restricted negation, which has received comparatively little attention in the existing literature. We demonstrate that this connective provides a natural and expressive basis for formulating the core principles of orthomodular logic. Furthermore, as a main result, we construct a new proof system for orthomodular logic founded on this connective.
item.dc:creator: Tomoaki Kawano (Kanagawa University), Ryo Kashima (Institute of Science Tokyo)

item.title: On {\L}ukasiewicz Topological Semantics
item.description: arXiv:2610.40809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose fuzzy topological semantics for {\L}ukasiewicz valued modal logic, based on the standard {\L}ukasiewicz algebra. Within this setting, formulas are interpreted as fuzzy sets of truth values, while the modal operators are realized through fuzzy interior and closure operators. We define a Kripke-induced fuzzy Alexandroff topology and establish a precise correspondence between {\L}ukasiewicz fuzzy Kripke semantics and its topological counterpart. The proposed topological semantics validates the S4 modal axioms that include reflexivity, transitivity, monotonicity, normality, and the necessitation of truth.
item.dc:creator: Muhammad Afaq Khan (CIDMA,Department of Mathematics, University of Aveiro Aveiro, Portugal), Manuel A. Martins (CIDMA,Department of Mathematics, University of Aveiro Aveiro, Portugal), Alexandre Madeira (CIDMA,Department of Mathematics, University of Aveiro Aveiro, Portugal), Babar Zaman (CIDMA,Department of Mathematics, University of Aveiro Aveiro, Portugal)

item.title: Merging and Evolution of Data Bases: A Many-Logic Approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.40812v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A new approach to information-based logics using many-logic modal structures (MLMSs) was recently proposed by Martins et al. In such a setting, it is possible to have worlds with different underlying logics within the same frame, all anchored to a base lattice that contains the semantics of each logic as a down-complete sublattice. In this paper, we take the lattice L6, defined by the six-valued semantics of the logic of evidence and truth LET + K , as our base lattice. We also consider four-, three-, and two-valued formal systems associated with down-complete sublattices of L6. These logics are capable of representing paracomplete, paraconsistent, and classical contexts with six, four, three, and two informational scenarios, respectively. As applications of MLMSs, we will discuss the merging and temporal evolution of databases whose underlying logics are two-, three-, four-, and six-valued. We will also investigate inconsistency measures in this context.
item.dc:creator: Manuel A. Martins (CIDMA,Dep. of Mathematics), Abilio Rodrigues (Federal University of Minas Gerais)

item.title: Restricted Peirce's Law and Natural Deduction
item.description: arXiv:2610.40813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The constructive logic JP' is known to be the weakest logic between intuitionistic and minimal logic that satisfies Glivenko's theorem. In spite of this natural and desirable formal property, the motivation for its notion of negation remains rather elusive: it can be characterised by a restriction of Peirce's law or by the double negation of ex falso quodlibet, neither of which is very intuitive. In order to have an alternative perspective on this negation, we study in this paper a couple of natural deduction systems for JP'. We first present a system that is normalisable and satisfies a restricted form of the subformula property. Then a modification of this system is introduced, whose rules satisfy the separation of connectives and the full subformula property. Afterwards we turn our attention to a typed lambda-calculus, with respect to which our natural deduction enjoys the Curry-Howard correspondence, followed by a concluding discussion.
item.dc:creator: Satoru Niki (Kanagawa University)

item.title: Paraclassical Logics with Two Negations
item.description: arXiv:2610.40814v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study three paraclassical propositional logics with two negations, CLoaN, CLouN, and CLauN, obtained by pairwise combining the one-negation systems CLuN, CLaN, and CLoN. CLuN's negation is glut-tolerant and paraconsistent, CLaN's negationis gap-tolerant and paracomplete, and CLoN's negation is both paraconsistent and paracomplete. We provide sound and complete two-valued non-deterministic semantics for each of the two-negations systems. We then focus on CLauN, the system containing the primitive dual pair of CLaN and CLuN negations. In this setting, we show deductive relationships between different negations expressible in CLauN; we show two diferent ways to recapture classical logic by means of translations, locally and globally; and we show a duality results for the multiple conclusion consequence relation of the logic.
item.dc:creator: Pawel Pawlowski (Centre for Logic,Philosophy of Science Ghent University, Ghent, Belgium), Pietro Vigiani (Institute of Computer Science Czech Academy of Sciences, Prague, Czech Republic Centre for Logic,Philosophy of Science Ghent University, Ghent, Belgium)

item.title: Normalisation for a Neutral Free Logic with Definite Descriptions
item.description: arXiv:2610.40816v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we present a natural deduction system for a strong Kleene-based neutral free logic with definite descriptions. The system combines a three-valued propositional basis with free quantification, identity, existence, and rules for definite descriptions. The main result is a normalisation theorem for a proof-theoretically equivalent restricted formulation of the system; we also establish a corresponding modified subformula property for its fragment.
item.dc:creator: Yaroslav Petrukhin (University of Lodz)

item.title: Cyclic Nonassociative Bilinear Logic With Additive Constants as Extension of Full Nonassociative Lambek Calculus
item.description: arXiv:2610.40817v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cyclic Linear Logic (CyMALL, CyBL) is a compromise between Commutative Linear Logic (MALL) and Noncommutative Linear Logic (Bilinear Logic, BL). We do not admit commutativity of the tensor, but we still admit only one De Morgan negation. MALL and its variants are natural extensions of Full Lambek Calculus (FL). Abrusci proved that CyBL is not a conservative extension of FL, if we admit additive constants in these logics. In this paper we show that Cyclic Nonassociative Bilinear Logic (CyNBL) with both additive constants is a strongly conservative extension of Full Nonassociative Lambek Calculus with only one additive constant - the upper bound - and that this holds even in the presence of an arbitrary set of nonlogical axioms.
item.dc:creator: Pawe{\l} P{\l}aczek (WSB Merito University in Poznan, Poland), Cheng-Syuan Wan (Tallinn University of Technology, Estonia)

item.title: Arithmetical Characterizations of Two Intuitionistic Logical Principles
item.description: arXiv:2610.40829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the role of negation in arithmetic by analyzing subsystems based on subminimal logic. We introduce NA^PR, a system of subminimal arithmetic equipped with all primitive recursive functions, and answer the following four questions: (1) Can we develop reasonable arithmetic within NA^PR? (2) Can we characterize logical rules Absorption of Negation (An) and Ex Falso Quodlibet (ECQ) by arithmetical principles? (3) Are there strict differences in deductive power among NA^PR, MA^PR, and HA? (4) Do MA^PR and MA, and NA^PR and NA have a similar mutual interpretability relationship as HA? We show the following: First, Heyting Arithmetic (HA) is shown to be a conservative extension of NA^PR for positive formulas. Based on NA^PR, we prove that (ECQ) is equivalent to the definability of disjunction, and that (An) is equivalent to a variant of the least number principle. Furthermore, using the constant domain neighbourhood semantics, we show that the systems NA^PR, MA^PR (written as NA^PR+(An)) and HA (written as NA^PR+(An)+(ECQ)) form a strictly increasing hierarchy of strength. Finally, we demonstrate the essential role of primitive recursive functions in weak arithmetic using classical countermodels.
item.dc:creator: Kaito Ichikura (Tohoku University)

item.title: Tableaux Rules for Theories of Definite Descriptions in Positive Free Logic with Some Philosophical Remarks
item.description: arXiv:2610.40830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While Russell's theory of definite descriptions, expressions of the form 'the F', is almost incontrovertible in classical logic, in free logic matters stand differently. Several alternatives have been proposed. In Lambert's hierarchy, the weakest theory is his minimal free theory of definite descriptions (MFD), which only says that anything is the F iff it is the unique existing F, the strongest one is a chosen object theory in which all improper definite descriptions refer to the same object (FD2). Intermediate is Lambert's FD1, which adds ix(x = t) = t as an axiom to MFD. MFD is very weak. FD2 is very strong. One might hope to find intermediate systems in which ix(x = t) = t is provable from more fundamental principles. The present paper considers one avenue where one might hope to find them and closes it. Two theories, FDA and FDH, will be considered that are motivated by considerations from proof-theoretic semantics. The former turns out to be equivalent to FD2, the latter to have unreasonable consequences. A third theory, similarly motivated, is also not viable. The philosophical upshot of this is briefly discussed.
item.dc:creator: Nils K\"urbis (University of {\L}\'od\'z)

item.title: DAPS: Dependency-Aware Premise Selection for LLM Theorem Proving
item.description: arXiv:2610.41536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-based theorem proving in Lean 4 has advanced rapidly, but provers are difficult to leverage newly contributed lemmas, because retrieval skews toward popular foundational lemmas, leaving the right premises buried among hundreds of thousands of candidates. Existing neural selectors rank candidates by semantic similarity, with three intrinsic limitations: frequency-skewed retrieval, isolated pairwise ranking, and degradation on out-of-distribution queries such as competition problems and informal language. Given that mathematics is structured by dependencies rather than similarities, we restore this signal to both the training data and the model. We curate two underused dependency resources. We conduct the first systematic mining of 53 Lean Blueprint projects, a previously untapped corpus of 3,805 manually curated informal+formal nodes that capture rare, research-level premises absent from Mathlib4. We further pair it with the extraction of comprehensive, typed, multi-level Mathlib4 dependencies. We then introduce DAPS, a dependency-aware premise selector with a structural neighborhood encoder, a group-level contrastive objective, and a Mathlib-then-Blueprint adaptation procedure. DAPS reaches mean Recall@32 of 89.25 on Mathlib4-Heldout (+11.41 over the strong selector LeanHammer), and maintains this lead on two out-of-distribution benchmarks. Further experiments demonstrate that DAPS premises improve theorem proving on miniF2F and IMO-ProofBench. Project page: https://daps-eth.github.io/.
item.dc:creator: Zixuan Chen, Wenyuan Jiang, Junling Wang, Mrinmaya Sachan, Yinya Huang

item.title: Pareto climate economics: optimism, pessimism and the polarization of societies
item.description: arXiv:2610.41832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We argue that simple conceptual models of the relation between short-term efforts in climate mitigation and adaptation policies (STECM&AP) and possible climate damages can help understanding the difficulties of increasing public support for a transition towards sustainable, decarbonized economies. Specifically, we show that, under fairly general conditions, mistrust and pessimism tend to polarize support for either minimal ``business as usual'' policies or maximal ``all-in climate mitigation efforts'' choices. Under the same conditions, trust and optimism tend to de-polarize societies towards moderate climate mitigation and adaptation (CM&A) policies and promote social consensus. If the relation between short-term efforts and possible climate damages can be quantified via empirical or model data, Pareto climate economics can be applied to extend these conceptual models and support climate decision making with trustable computational methods.
item.dc:creator: Nicola Botta, Patrik Jansson, Tim Richter

item.title: Type classifiers
item.description: arXiv:2610.41941v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend dependent type theory by type classifiers and construct an interpretation in the category of contextual categories with families. Type classifiers extend contexts by type variables, complementing the usual context extensions by term variables of specified types. This allows statements with arbitrary type parameters to be formulated without assuming a universe. We show that substituting isomorphic types induces isomorphisms between the resulting types even in extensional type theory, giving an analogue of the invariance supplied by the univalence axiom in homotopy type theory. Omitting function types from the theory, so that all type formers are covariant, extends this naturality to arbitrary, possibly noninvertible maps.
item.dc:creator: Martin E. Bidlingmaier

item.title: Model Checking for Metric Extensions of Monadic Second-Order Logic
item.description: arXiv:2610.41974v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Monadic second-order logic yields powerful algorithmic meta-theorems, but cannot express that a vertex set induces a shortest path. We study metric extensions of counting monadic second-order logic and identify structural parameters supporting efficient model checking, optimization, and counting. We show that shortest paths and equidistance guarded by geodesic cycles are definable in ordinary vertex-set MSO on graph classes of bounded cycle-basis length. This yields fixed-parameter tractable model checking for the corresponding extensions of CMSO2, parameterized by formula length and bag-connected treewidth, and of CMSO1, parameterized by formula length and geodesic cliquewidth: the sum of cliquewidth and cycle-basis length. The translations preserve free variables, yielding additive optimization and counting. Applications include Minimum Geodetic Set and Strong Metric Dimension for geodesic cliquewidth, and Minimum Isometric Path Partition for bag-connected treewidth. We also introduce restricted packing-covering templates that allow numerical distance thresholds to remain outside the parameter. For each fixed template, feasibility, additive vertex-weight optimization, and counting are fixed-parameter tractable in bag-connected treewidth. Applications include Distance-r Dominating Set, d-Scattered Set, and Minimum Eccentricity Shortest Path. Finally, we characterize bounded bag-connected treewidth and bounded geodesic cliquewidth through monadic dependence for the corresponding guarded logics. Unguarded distance comparisons have stricter structural boundaries: first-order model checking is AW[*]-complete already on uncolored caterpillars, and model checking a fixed existential monadic sentence is NP-complete on this class.
item.dc:creator: Dibyayan Chakraborty, Sebastian Ordyniak, Sebastian Siebertz

item.title: General semiring conditions for weighted L* termination
item.description: arXiv:2610.41184v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Weighted automata learning has been well-studied over (semi)rings which have a dimension theory. In this work, we investigate active learning for weighted automata over semirings that lack such a structure. We first show that the principal ideal domain variant of the L* algorithm also terminates for a larger class of semirings containing Noetherian semirings, commutative rings, and bounded distributed lattices. We then present a variant of this algorithm for learning deterministic weighted automata, and prove that this algorithm terminates for commutative semirings.
item.dc:creator: Noah Bertram, Daniel Luckhardt, Alexandra Silva

item.title: Propositional Dynamic Logic has Craig Interpolation: a tableau-based proof
item.description: arXiv:2503.13276v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that Propositional Dynamic Logic (PDL) has the Craig Interpolation Property. This question has been open for many years. Three proof attempts were published, but later criticized in the literature or retracted. Our proof is based on the main ideas from Borzechowski (1988, master thesis). We define a cyclic tableau system for PDL with a loading mechanism to recognize successful repeats. For this system, we show soundness and completeness via a game. To show interpolation, we modify Maehara's method to work for tableaux with repeats: we first define pre-interpolants at each node, and then use a quasi-tableau to define interpolants for clusters (strongly connected components). In different terms, our method solves the fixpoint equations that characterize the desired interpolants, and the method ensures that the solutions to these equations can be expressed within PDL. The proof is constructive and we show how to compute interpolants. We make available a Haskell implementation of the proof system that provides interpolants, and a formal verification of our proof in the interactive theorem prover Lean. Lastly, we discuss several questions for future work.
item.dc:creator: Manfred Borzechowski, Malvin Gattinger, Helle Hvid Hansen, Revantha Ramanayake, Francisco Trucco Dalmas, Yde Venema

item.title: Decidability in First-Order Modal Logic with Non-Rigid Constants and Definite Descriptions
item.description: arXiv:2509.08165v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: While modal extensions of decidable fragments of first-order logic are usually undecidable, their monodic counterparts, in which formulas in the scope of modal operators have at most one free variable, are typically decidable. This only holds, however, under the provision that non-rigid constants, definite descriptions and non-trivial counting are not admitted. Indeed, several monodic fragments having at least one of these features are known to be undecidable. We investigate these features systematically and show that fundamental monodic fragments such as the two-variable fragment with counting and the guarded fragment of standard first-order modal logics $\mathbf{K}_{n}$ and $\mathbf{S5}_{n}$ are decidable. Tight complexity bounds are established as well. Under the expanding-domain semantics, we show decidability of the basic modal logic extended with the transitive closure operator on frames without infinite ascending chains; this logic, however, is Ackermann-hard.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Artale, Christopher Hampson, Roman Kontchakov, Andrea Mazzullo, Frank Wolter

item.title: Coalgebraic Non-Wellfounded Proofs: Recursiveness and GTC
item.description: arXiv:2605.15664v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Non-wellfounded proof systems impose a global condition called the global trace condition (GTC) on a derivation tree to ensure soundness. Providing a categorical characterisation of the GTC that guarantees soundness remains challenging due to the global, non-compositional nature of these conditions and the infinitary structure of non-wellfounded proofs. We develop a coalgebraic framework for non-wellfounded proof systems where derivation trees are modelled as coalgebras of generalised polynomial functors on presheaves. Since the GTC is a constraint on infinite paths in derivation graphs, we employ graphs of coalgebras and formulate the GTC coalgebraically as a condition on these graphs. Soundness is then formulated as the existence of a unique coalgebra-to-algebra morphism from a coalgebra representing a derivation graph to an algebra specifying semantics. Within this framework, we characterise the GTC via recursive coalgebras: a coalgebra satisfies the GTC if and only if its ordinal-annotated image is recursive for every ordinal bound. For semantic algebras obtained from annotated algebras by the induced right-adjoint lifting, this yields soundness: every proof admits a unique coalgebra-to-algebra morphism in the original proof system. We demonstrate the framework through a non-wellfounded proof system for the modal mu-calculus and a non-wellfounded variant of Santocanale's circular proof system in mu-bicomplete categories.
item.dc:creator: Mayuko Kori

item.title: A Hybrid SMT-NRA Solver: Integrating 2D Cell-Jump-Based Local Search, MCSAT and OpenCAD
item.description: arXiv:2507.00557v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we propose a hybrid framework for Satisfiability Modulo the Theory of Nonlinear Real Arithmetic (SMT-NRA for short). First, we introduce a two-dimensional cell-jump move, called \emph{2D-cell-jump}, generalizing the key operation, cell-jump, of the local search method for SMT-NRA. In contrast to the existing cell-jump, which updates assignments exclusively along a given line, the 2D-cell-jump enables search over an arbitrarily selected plane. Then, we propose an extended local search framework, named \emph{2D-LS} (following the existing local search framework, LS, for SMT-NRA). Finally, we present a hybrid framework for SMT-NRA integrating 2D-LS, MCSAT and OpenCAD, to improve search efficiency through information exchange. The experimental results demonstrate improvements in local search performance, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed methods.
item.dc:creator: Tianyi Ding, Haokun Li, Xinpeng Ni, Bican Xia, Tianqi Zhao

item.title: h1: A Taste of the Bitter Lesson in Automated Theorem Proving
item.description: arXiv:2610.35962v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: While progress in informal mathematics has come largely from scaling the chain-of-thought and agentic reasoning of frontier language models, formal theorem proving has increasingly relied on human-designed workflows around these models, such as planning, decomposition, and orchestrating specialized provers. This raises a bitter-lesson question: can a simple agentic loop that scales test-time compute match these workflows? The answer matters as formal verification must scale to keep up with frontier models producing research mathematics, yet new workflows rarely settle it, as their gains are often confounded with stronger models or more compute. We study this question with h1, a simple harness that gives a model an efficient interface to Lean 4 and keeps it working through verifier feedback and self-reflection, without imposing a decomposition or search structure. h1 reaches state-of-the-art results on PutnamBench, FATE-X, and FormalConjectures100-Solved, settles eight open problems in FormalConjectures, and, at matched models, matches or outperforms specialized workflows such as Goedel-Architect and AlphaProof Nexus, surprisingly showing that a single attempt (pass@1) can often scale to solve open problems. Through ablations and matched-model comparisons with Claude Code and AxProverBase, we find that simplicity alone is not enough: an efficient Lean interface largely determines cost and solve rate. We thus recommend that future work evaluate frontier models with efficient execution feedback before prescribing workflows, at the risk of bitter lessons.
item.dc:creator: Skander Moalla, Ahmad Rammal, Niket Patel, Remi Munos, Julia Kempe

item.title: Algebraic World Model: From Exploration to Proofs
item.description: arXiv:2610.40503v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: AI has made remarkable progress in mathematics, solving challenging problems with machine-checkable proofs in Lean, yet typically relying on predefined mathematical definitions and formal specifications. This raises a natural question: can it reason rigorously about an unknown world? We introduce the Algebraic World Model (AWM), a framework that turns interaction with unfamiliar environments into explicit mathematical models supporting formal reasoning. AWM explores the environment and develops executable Python hypotheses, continually testing and revising them against observations. It then structures these hypotheses into typed objects and shared rules, simplifies their structure through category-theory-guided transformations, and formalizes the resulting model in Lean 4 to prove reachability and impossibility. AWM can formally prove that a goal is unreachable, even beyond explored trajectories. On two impossible game levels, it constructs closed, kernel-checked Lean proofs excluding every legal winning sequence in all six runs, while Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, equipped with coding tools, produce none in twelve baseline runs. Four of AWM's six initial bounds are correct, compared with one for Opus 5.5 and none for GPT-6 Astra; given only feedback that a cheaper win exists, AWM revises its rules and constructs new proofs, reaching six of six correct bounds. Moreover, AWM produces interpretable mathematical models whose rules can be inspected and tested step by step. Across all 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games, these models enable Lean to replay the winning trajectories of all 183 levels and generalize beyond observed play, predicting unseen transitions and detecting changes in game mechanics. With Claude Opus 5, AWM clears all levels with a score of 99.9, while its certified winning trajectories use only 43% of the human baseline's actions.
item.dc:creator: Guancheng Pan, Qixin Tan, Yang Yuan, Andrew Chi-Chih Yao
